summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and a history of alcohol and benzodiazepine use, was re-admitted after leaving against medical advice the prior day. He presented with hemoptysis and chest pain, and imaging confirmed a pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe with likely infarct and a small to moderate pleural effusion. Despite being hemodynamically stable, he again insisted on leaving the hospital. Due to his prior failure to use prescribed anticoagulation and ongoing substance use, he was not discharged on blood thinners, as it was deemed unsafe. Psychiatry confirmed he had decision-making capacity. He was discharged home on his baseline medications with strong warnings about the life-threatening risk of untreated pulmonary embolism and instructions to seek immediate care if symptoms worsened.
